Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Japamala Das Mahapatra
& Ors on 7 May, 2024

In The High Court At Calutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 07.05. 2024
 Sl No.2.
Court No.25

Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.
 Vs.
 Japamala Das Mahapatra & Ors.
 Ms. Gopa Das Mukherjee,
 ......for the appellants.

Mr. Amit Ranjan Roy,
 ......for the respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Mr. Jayanta Kr. Mondal, ......for the respondent no. 4.

The instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment and award dated 18th January, 2023,
passed by the learned MAC Tribunal cum Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 3rd Court, Paschim Medinipur, in MAC Case no. 576 of 2016.

entities.text: MAC Tribunal cum Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 3rd Court, Paschim Medinipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief fact of the case is that, the victim of this case namely one Debanjan Das Mahapatra on 29.10.20216 at about 03.05 P.M. was travelling from Makrampur to his house at Belda boarding by Scopio car Bearing no. WB -20G/4121 along with his relatives and friends.

The said scorpio was running in very a high speed in rash and negligent manner and when they reached at Poktapole at the Bake more on HN-60 under P.S. Narayangarh, the said scorpio capsized beside the road and by such accident the victim sustained severe injuries and succumbed to his injury during his treatment at Medinipur Medical College and Hospital.

One claim application was filed by the parents and widow of the deceased before the learned Tribunal vide an application under Section 166 of M.V. Act for getting compensation on the ground that the victim died due to rash and negligent negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle (scorpio) duly insured under the policy of the Insurance Company.
The claimant's case was contested by the Insurance Company by filing written statement.

After hearing the parties and after receiving the evidence, the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 41,46,200/- together with 6% per annum in favour of the claimants and directed the Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Japamala Das Mahapatra & Ors on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179144717/
1 Insurance Company to the pay the compensation to the mother and widow of the deceased equally.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award the Insurance Company has preferred the instant appeal.

sentences.text: Ms. Mukherjee, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company submits that the instant appeal is preferred challenging the award passed by the learned Tribunal only on the ground of quantum of compensation.
Ms. Mukherjee submits that learned Tribunal has erroneously fixed the income of the deceased on the basis of ITR 2016-17.
She submits that the ITR filed by the deceased for the assessment year 2016-17 contained the name of business as D.D. Enterprise.
No document of such D.D. enterprise was produced before the learned Tribunal to show the name of the business.
He further argued that the claim application stated the business of deceased as transport business and the owner of a passenger bus.
She further argued that PW-3 that is the Income Tax Officer deposed and stated that the ITR were self-assessed ITR and the Income Tax Department did not verify the containts of those ITR.
She submits that learned Tribunal has erroneously assessed the income of the deceased on the basis of the ITR 2016-17.
Ms. Mukherjee further argued that learned Tribunal has awarded filial consortium in favour of the mother of the victim.
She submits by virtue of the Hon'ble Apex Court decision in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, the widow of the deceased is only entitled to get consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ms. Mukherjee further argued that the claimants are not entitle to get interest of future prospect.

She submits that in this case future prospect was awarded 40%
considering the age of the deceased but the entire compensation was directed to carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
She submits that the observation of the learned Tribunal regarding awarding interest upon the future prospect is not proper.
In support of her contention she cited the decisions of Hon'ble Gauhati High Court in I. Nasima Begum Vs. Keramat Ali and Ors. and II.Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smti Champabati Ray and Ors.

sentences.text: Mr. Roy, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the parents of the deceased submits that the ITR were duly exhibited through the PW-3. PW- 3 is Officer of the Income Tax Department who identify and filed the certified copy of the Income Tax return for the assessment year 2014-15, 2015- 16, and 2016-17.
Mr. Roy further argued that the consecutive filing of ITR itself proved the running business of the deceased.
Mr. Roy submits, it is quite unreasonable for a person to submit the regular return with supposition that those return would be used in a future claim case.
He further argued that learned Tribunal has correctly assessed the compensation in this case by virtue of ITR for the assessment year 2016-17.

Mr. Mondal, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the widow of the deceased submits that the verification of the ITR is within the domain of the I.T. Department, if there is any discrepancy in the return it is duty of the I.T. Department to issue a notice to the assessee.
No such evidence has been adduced that any discrepancy was appeared to the Income Tax Department.
He further pointed out several imputs in the said ITR and submits that the necessary tax liability was calculated on the basis of income of the said firm owned by the deceased.
He submits that ITR with the assessment year 2016-17 is beyond doubt so it can be considered for assessing the income of the deceased.

He further submits that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Smt. Anjali & Ors. vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors.
reported in 2023 SAR (civil) 2018 has considered the Income Tax Return for a single assessment year which was disbelieved by the Tribunal as well as the Hon'ble High Court concerned.

sentences.text: Heard the learned Counsel and perused the materials-on-record and also perused the evidence as placed before this Court through the paper book.
The income of the deceased is the sole challenge of the Insurance Company before the Appellate Court.
The learned Tribunal has assessed the compensation on the basis of the income of the deceased in the assessment year 2016-17.
The income tax return of the deceased filed before the concerned I.T Department for the assessment year 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17 were marked as exhibit 11 collectively.

On perusal of the income tax return for the assessment year 2016-17, it appears that said income tax return was filed on 3rd June,
2016 ; alleged accident happened on 29th October, 2016.
So, it appears that this is the last income tax filed by the deceased prior to his accident.
At the first page of the income tax return, the nature of business or profession mentioned trade name as mentioned D.D. Enterprise.

Ms. Mukherjee,
argued that the name of the business is not transpiring either in the claim application or in the evidence of PW-1 (father of the deceased), she further pointed out written submission of widow who also not disclosed about the business of her husband through D.D. Enterprise.
Though these points were argued by appellant, but the same was not enquired or questioned by the Insurance Company to PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 i.e., the witnesses of the claimants.
No evidence were produced either oral and documentary by the Insurance Company to prove the nature and avocation of the deceased in this case is otherwise than pleaded.

It appears to me that by the decision in Hon'ble Supreme Court in Malarvizhi Vs. United India Insurance Companyu Ltd., the income tax return is a statutory document and reliance can be placed upon this statutory document to assess income of the deceased.

The income tax return is a statutory document on which reliance may be placed to determine the annual income of the deceased.

1,18,261/-aprox. Rs. 9,855/- per month keeping in mind the deceased's Income Tax Return for the year 2009-2010."

Considering the observation I find no justification to enquire into the name business that is D.D.
Enterprise at this appellate stage and its applicability in claim case.
I find no justification to disbelieve the finding of the learned Tribunal in respect of assessing the income of the deceased on the basis of ITR for the assessment year 2016-17.

It appears that the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs. 44,000/- as a loss spousal consortium also Rs.
44,000/-as a loss of filial consortium.
In this case the learned Tribunal had directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation towards consortium to the widow as well as the mother of the deceased.
So filial consortium of Rs. 44,000/- in favour of the mother of the deceased was awarded.
Mr. Mondal submits that the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Satinder Kaur (supra) as well as Nanuram (supra), the spousal consortium as well as filial consortium has been considered.

The issue of awarding Filial consortium and parental consortium is under active considered in a separate appeal, till deciding the issue this Court has on several occasion has ordered that the consortium can only be awarded in favour of the widow of the deceased by virtue of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Pranay Sethi

, I think it is necessary to hold that in this case learned Tribunal has awarded the consortium in favour of Satindra Kaur (supra), but by virtue of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) comprising the five Judges Bench, widow of the deceased is only entitle to get the consortium amounting to Rs. 40,000/- further it increased can be 10% after every three years; thus in this case the award of Filial consortium in favour of the mother of deceased appears to be not justified.
It has argued by the learned Counsel for the Insurance Company that future prospect would not carry further interest.

He cited the decision of Coordinate Bench of Gauhati High Court passed in Nasima Begum (supra) wherein the Coordinate Bench has observed that the appellant will not be entitled to get interest on and upon the future prospect, but was calculated future prospect 25% and the Coordinate Bench has also order that the total compensation shall carry 6% interest per annum.
Another Coordinate Bench of the Gauhati High Court in Smiti Champabati (supra) has followed the observation of Nasima Begum.

In considering the observation of the Coordinate Benchs of Gauhati High Court, it appears to me that the finding and observation of the Hon'ble Coordinate Bench appears to be justified on the ground that the assessment of compensation on the different heads are different components which come under the purview of a total compensation awarded under the provision under Section 166 of MV Act.
The statute under Section 171 of MV Act has specifically enumerated that of compensation shall carry interest from the date of filing of the claim application.

In this case the future prospect as directed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) is only acomponent of total compensation which could not be calculated separately thus the observation of Gauhati High Court regarding future prospect its applicability in case under Section 166 of M.V. Act to be no justified.
Considering the aspect the award passed by the learned Tribunal requires modification only on the basis of the award filial consortium of Rs. 44,000/- .

The total award passed by the learned Tribunal Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Japamala Das Mahapatra & Ors on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179144717/
4 is of Rs. 44,46,200/- from which Rs. 44,000/- would be deducted ; thus award comes to Rs.
41,42,200/-.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has directed to pay awarded amount together with 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application that is from 14.12.2016 till payment.

It appears that Insurance Company has initially deposited Rs. 25,000/- again deposited Rs. 55,45,447/- and Rs. 3,54,687/- on 12.3.2024 separately ; total amount the Insurance Company thus deposited Rs. 59,54,634/-.

The Office of the learned Registrar General, Calcutta High Court is directed to calculate the award together with the interest and disburse the same in the name of the mother and widow of the deceased equally.
After such disbursement there may have some residue in the account of the Insurance Company, the same along with the accrued interest be refunded to the Insurance Company.
The payment of compensation is subject to ascertainment of the payment of deficit Court fee, if any.
The learned Tribunal shall act upon certified copy of this order to receive the deficit Court fee, in any.
LCR be sent down at once, if already received.
The instant FMA 519 of 2023 all connected applications, if any, are disposed of.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
Parties to act upon the server copy and urgent certified copy of this order be provided on usual terms and conditions.

(Subhendu Samanta, J.)
